transcription.text: [music]
[speaking Chinese]
English student's book 4b
Page 1. Unit 1. What is your daily schedule?
Page 2. Get ready.
A. Listen. Then point and say.
What do you do every day?
I get up at 7am. I have breakfast at 7.30am.
I go to school at 8am. I have lunch at 11.30am.
I go home at 4.30pm. I have dinner at 6pm.
I go to bed at 9pm.
Page 4. Explore. Li Ming's and Li Liang's day.
1. Hi. I'm Li Ming. I get up at 7 o'clock every day.
I brush my teeth and wash my face.
Then I have breakfast. I go to school at half past 7.
What time does Li Liang get up?
My little brother Li Liang gets up at 8 o'clock.
Then he drinks some milk.
2. I have 4 lessons in the morning. I read books and work with my
friends.
Li Liang likes drawing pictures.
What time does Li Ming come home?
Page 5. 3. I get home at a quarter to 5.
I play with my brother. 4. I read a story to Li Liang at a quarter to 9.
5. We go to bed at 9 o'clock. Good night, kids.
P L, pl, play. B L, bl, blue.
Page 7. C. Listen and chant. My friend Anne's day.
My friend Anne is busy every day. What time does she get up?
She gets up at a quarter to 7. She brushes her teeth. She washes her
face. She eats at 7 o'clock.
It's time for school. She checks her bag.
Oh, look at the clock. It's a quarter to 8. Hurry up, Anne. You'll be
late.
Learn. What time does she get up? She gets up at a quarter to 7. Get,
gets, do, does, have, has.
Page 8. Communicate. A. Listen and draw. Then say.
Mr. Li is Li Ming and Li Liang's uncle. Every morning, he gets up at
half past 6. He goes to work at a quarter to 8. He begins to work at 8
o'clock. He gets home at 9 o'clock in the evening and plays with his
pet cat.
He goes to bed at half past 10. He's busy, but he's happy every day.
Page 10. Extend. Jaja needs a schedule. At home. One. Jaja, it's 9 p.m.
Go to bed now. Alright, Mum. Two. Get up, Jaja.
Five more minutes, please. Hurry up. There's no time for breakfast. Mum,
I'm sleepy. At the bus stop. Three. Hurry up, Jaja. The school bus is
coming.
Okay. Oh no, Jaja. You missed the school bus. In the classroom. Four.
Good morning, Mr. Yen. Sorry, I'm late. The next day. Five. Oh, you're
on time today. Good.
I don't want to be late again.
